main_theorems.title: The period, its exact domain, and its arithmetic norm
main_theorems.label: series:I:A

steps.claim_tex:
The pointed maps
$(x,y)\mapsto(2x,-2\sqrt2y)$ and
$(x_0,y_0)\mapsto(-x_0,y_0/(2i))$ transport the chosen section,
invariant differential and period lattice.  The quotient
exponential identifies the period model with the elliptic-surface
line-bundle quotient
(\hyperref[I:weierstrass-comparison]{\ref*{I:weierstrass-comparison}},
\hyperref[fam:src:B.1.1]{\ref*{fam:src:B.1.1}}).

The two theta transformation
factors give the prescribed affine period laws; the cusp product
fixes the additive constant and hence the displayed logarithm
(\hyperref[fam:src:C.1.1]{\ref*{fam:src:C.1.1}}).

The distribution identity gives
the exact division-polynomial norm formula, and $mP=\pm P$
cancels the remaining norm.  The stated polynomial roots and
values then determine every order-four-through-eight
specialization
(\hyperref[ari:C.4.2]{\ref*{ari:C.4.2}},
\hyperref[ari:C.4.3]{\ref*{ari:C.4.3}},
\hyperref[ari:C.4.4]{\ref*{ari:C.4.4}}).

Exact polynomial bounds away
from the square root point and the controlled local theta
expansion give $\max N=\sqrt2$.  The determinant identity and
its cusp limit then give exactly $\Im c<H_*$
(\hyperref[ari:C.8.1]{\ref*{ari:C.8.1}},
\hyperref[ari:C.8.2]{\ref*{ari:C.8.2}},
\hyperref[ari:C.8.3]{\ref*{ari:C.8.3}},
\hyperref[ari:C.8.4]{\ref*{ari:C.8.4}},
\hyperref[fam:src:C.2.3]{\ref*{fam:src:C.2.3}}).

The normalized critical factor
satisfies $|1-X|<1$ and
$(t-1)L_t=X(X-2)/24$.  Its radial sign, the coarse derivative
at zero and the cusp limit give the complete critical and level
classification
(\hyperref[ari:C.8.15]{\ref*{ari:C.8.15}},
\hyperref[push:src:D.4.8]{\ref*{push:src:D.4.8}}).

The local multiplication identity
evaluates every finite-place contribution on the stated minimal
models.  The product formula identifies the archimedean term and
gives the eleven exact CM factors
(\hyperref[ari:C.6.1]{\ref*{ari:C.6.1}},
\hyperref[ari:C.6.3]{\ref*{ari:C.6.3}}).

main_theorems.title: All discrete data, the parameter, and real forms
main_theorems.label: series:I:B

steps.claim_tex:
The intrinsic canonical pencil
fixes the base.  Its period centralizer forces $c'-c\in\Z$ and
the fibre-linear part $aI_2$
(\hyperref[fam:src:A.1.1]{\ref*{fam:src:A.1.1}},
\hyperref[fam:src:A.5.1]{\ref*{fam:src:A.5.1}}).

Solving the two finite norm
equations gives the parity condition; comparing the actual cusp
collar gives $p'=ap$.  The holomorphic correction solves the
remaining gluing, so these necessary equations are sufficient
(\hyperref[fam:src:B.2.1]{\ref*{fam:src:B.2.1}},
\hyperref[fam:src:B.2.2]{\ref*{fam:src:B.2.2}},
\hyperref[fam:src:B.2.3]{\ref*{fam:src:B.2.3}}).

The higher root pullbacks multiply
the norm images by $k,l$, yielding exactly the congruences modulo
$k,2l$.  Their intersection is $2kl\Z$, and a positive $u$
circuit is the cyclic parameter translation
(\hyperref[fam:src:B.3.1]{\ref*{fam:src:B.3.1}},
\hyperref[push:src:E.1.2]{\ref*{push:src:E.1.2}}).

The invariant-coordinate lattice,
including its affine half-period, and the two exact finite theta
values give the Albanese nomes
(\hyperref[ari:C.2.1]{\ref*{ari:C.2.1}}).

The explicit reflected period
and affine lattice maps give $c'\equiv1-\bar c\pmod{2\Z}$.
Their square and holomorphic conjugacy identify the two
involution classes
(\hyperref[fam:src:B.4.2]{\ref*{fam:src:B.4.2}},
\hyperref[mapsI:src:A.3.1]{\ref*{mapsI:src:A.3.1}}).

The fixed-lift congruences and
cusp units determine the nonempty pieces.  The exact cap-meridian
matrices close them to $S^3$ and determine the semifree or Hopf
circle action
(\hyperref[mapsI:src:A.3.2]{\ref*{mapsI:src:A.3.2}},
\hyperref[mapsI:src:A.3.3]{\ref*{mapsI:src:A.3.3}}).

main_theorems.title: The monodromy quotient and every fibre's algebraic dimension
main_theorems.label: series:I:C

steps.claim_tex:
The parabolic multiplication law
and the polarization of $x_1+x_2+x_1x_2$ prove the character law.
The commutator and its conjugates generate its integral kernel,
giving the two exact indices
(\hyperref[fam:src:F.1.1]{\ref*{fam:src:F.1.1}}).

Actual modular lifts first reduce
the Iwasawa factor, integral Heisenberg translations reduce $x$,
and the center reduces $t$.  Interior uniqueness and the displayed
face maps give the fundamental set
(\hyperref[I:monodromy-fundamental-set]{\ref*{I:monodromy-fundamental-set}}).

Real parabolic stabilizers are
compact on $q_d\ne0$.  Rational parabolic conjugates of the
explicit null unipotent give a dense infinite-stabilizer locus,
which proves maximality
(\hyperref[fam:src:F.2.2]{\ref*{fam:src:F.2.2}},
\hyperref[fam:src:F.2.3]{\ref*{fam:src:F.2.3}}).

The modular function $j/1728$
is the period map's left inverse, while the finite root charts
extend it at zero and one.  Its control on compact inverse
images proves properness on the finite $t$-line
(\hyperref[fam:src:F.3.1]{\ref*{fam:src:F.3.1}}).

Wedge the period rows with an
integral alternating form to obtain the exact $(1,1)$ equation.
Its Hermitian determinant and the complex orientation give
$E^2=-2\operatorname{Pf}(E)$ and the quotient/projectivity tests
(\hyperref[fam:src:D.1.4]{\ref*{fam:src:D.1.4}},
\hyperref[fam:src:D.1.6]{\ref*{fam:src:D.1.6}}).

main_theorems.title: Cohomology and the ordinary relative differential modules
main_theorems.label: series:I:D

steps.claim_tex:
Root characters and the cusp
normalization compute the logarithmic direct images.  The residue
connecting map is evaluated as an actual nonzero scalar, fixing
the remaining Hodge integer at one
(\hyperref[inv:A2.2]{\ref*{inv:A2.2}},
\hyperref[inv:A2.4]{\ref*{inv:A2.4}}).

Coherent Leray on the curve,
the structure-sheaf inputs and Serre duality give the complete
Dolbeault table, uniformly for every admissible parameter
(\hyperref[inv:A1.0]{\ref*{inv:A1.0}},
\hyperref[inv:A3.1]{\ref*{inv:A3.1}}).

The middle rows and the
$S^6$ de Rham groups force the four rank-one differentials.
The double-complex decomposition then gives the Bott--Chern and
Aeppli tables and the explicitly checked square-zero products
(\hyperref[inv:C1.1]{\ref*{inv:C1.1}},
\hyperref[inv:C2.1]{\ref*{inv:C2.1}},
\hyperref[inv:C3.3]{\ref*{inv:C3.3}}).

Quotienting by $dt$ gives the
degree-one modules.  The maps $(a,b,c)\mapsto(xa-zc,yb-zc)$
and $\Omega^2\xrightarrow{\wedge dt}I$ compute their kernels
and torsion exactly; finite etale descent gives the global
support assertion
(\hyperref[inv:A4.1]{\ref*{inv:A4.1}},
\hyperref[inv:A4.2]{\ref*{inv:A4.2}}).

main_theorems.title: Every Picard twist and the deformation parameter
main_theorems.label: series:I:E

steps.claim_tex:
The primitive Picard
normalization identifies the integer twists, and weighted
coarse degrees give their section counts and four dimensions
(\hyperref[inv:C3.2]{\ref*{inv:C3.2}},
\hyperref[inv:D4.1]{\ref*{inv:D4.1}}).

The actual integral cocycle
modulo the two period rows gives the regular resonance equation
and both finite root lattices.  At the cusp the normalization
complex gives exactly the reduced degree-two skyscraper
(\hyperref[inv:D4.2]{\ref*{inv:D4.2}},
\hyperref[inv:D4.3]{\ref*{inv:D4.3}}).

The joint order-three
coefficient $123ik/(64\pi)$ fixes the local normal form;
Smith modules and every stabilizer character give the complete
finite stalk lengths.  Leray then gives the formula for $J_z$
(\hyperref[inv:D4.4]{\ref*{inv:D4.4}},
\hyperref[inv:D4.5]{\ref*{inv:D4.5}}).

The established
$\bar\partial$-closed form $G_\gamma=G_0/12$ defines the
Picard family by $\bar\partial-2\pi izG_\gamma$.
Proper coherent base change and a real nonintegral nonresonant
point make every actual jump locus locally discrete
(\hyperref[inv:C3.1]{\ref*{inv:C3.1}},
\hyperref[inv:C3.2]{\ref*{inv:C3.2}},
\hyperref[inv:D4.5]{\ref*{inv:D4.5}}).

The root-forgetting map
$(x,y)\mapsto(x^l,y^k)$ with character
$\lambda\mapsto\lambda^{kl}$ pulls back the standard Hodge
line.  Its weighted direct images and logarithmic tangent
sequence give $(1,1,1,0)$ for every stated higher sphere member
(\hyperref[push:src:E.1.2]{\ref*{push:src:E.1.2}},
\hyperref[push:src:E.2.1]{\ref*{push:src:E.2.1}}).

Differentiating the actual
period groupoid gives the nonzero class $e\otimes[\gamma]$.
The induced parameter map forces the one-variable Kuranishi
ring to be reduced and smooth.  The integral translation sheaf
gives the standard automorphism group
(\hyperref[fam:st:A.5.2]{\ref*{fam:st:A.5.2}},
\hyperref[fam:src:B.4.1]{\ref*{fam:src:B.4.1}},
\hyperref[push:src:E.2.1]{\ref*{push:src:E.2.1}}).

main_theorems.title: The puncture and the obstruction to every proper filling
main_theorems.label: series:I:F

steps.claim_tex:
The node charts
$X_i=W/r^i$, $Y_i=r^{i+1}/W$, $X_iY_i=r$ and their inverse
overlaps give the proper rank-one cycle.  The finite affine
actions rotate its components freely and produce the stated
cover.  Subtraction of the actual two origins fixes both deck
differences
(\hyperref[night:P2.2]{\ref*{night:P2.2}},
\hyperref[night:P2.3]{\ref*{night:P2.3}}).

Resolve a proposed filling's
dominating component.  Its relative anticanonical direct image
recovers the pencil, and the three labelled critical-value
sections recover the marked base by their meromorphic cross-ratio
(\hyperref[night:P2.4]{\ref*{night:P2.4}}).

Modulo $\widehat\delta$ the
actual cross-cocycles vanish.  The three unipotent annihilator
equations have determinant 6; Stein factorization on a horizontal
central component then kills its normal-meridian class
(\hyperref[night:P2.5]{\ref*{night:P2.5}},
\hyperref[night:P2.6]{\ref*{night:P2.6}}).

Principalization makes both
axes normal crossing.  The Stein finite factor is birational
over the normal bidisc, so the compact corner fibre is connected.
The lifts $Q_o=T_{-mb\widehat\gamma}Q$, $R_o=R$ commute;
local meridians therefore satisfy the constant-ratio equation
(\hyperref[night:P2.7]{\ref*{night:P2.7}}).

The connected incidence graph
joins a horizontal ratio zero to the strict cusp ratio $a$.
Admissibility gives $\gcd(a,12)=1$, producing the contradiction
for every proper analytic filling and every finite cover
(\hyperref[night:P2.7]{\ref*{night:P2.7}}).

For higher multiplicities,
$K_X^{-N}=f^*\mathcal O(4l+3k-kl)$ with nonzero degree.
The positive canonical power and its three labelled critical
points recover the degree-one base parameter.  The same ratio
argument and $\gcd(a,N)=1$ give the full higher conclusion
(\hyperref[night:P2.9]{\ref*{night:P2.9}}).

With zero logarithmic
translations the two line-bundle neck equations have zero
corner winding and give the proper flat plumbing after its
specified modification and finite quotient.  Normalization and
the double-locus smoothing formula give virtual Euler zero for
Engel's particular one-component proposal, excluding its
smoothing to $e=2$
(\hyperref[night:P2.10]{\ref*{night:P2.10}},
\hyperref[night:P2.11]{\ref*{night:P2.11}}).

main_theorems.title: The outer boundary and all marked additive limits
main_theorems.label: series:I:G

steps.claim_tex:
The canonical divisor recovers
$S_2$ intrinsically in a proper extension.  Its normalization
and Albanese invariant retain $J(iw/216)$, whose natural boundary
excludes crossing the outer circle
(\hyperref[push:src:D.1.3]{\ref*{push:src:D.1.3}}).

The fixed complex-linear and
integral basis changes give the displayed four periods.
The local theta expansion gives $B(h)=-3ih^2+O(h^4)$ and
the exact inverse transpose gives every integral dual covector
(\hyperref[push:src:D.2.1]{\ref*{push:src:D.2.1}},
\hyperref[eq:d-dual-exact]{\ref*{eq:d-dual-exact}}).

Bounded dual covectors have
constant integral labels after subselection; their labels form
$L_a$.  The quadratic real term cancels, leaving
$\lambda\cdot V_n+o(1)$.  The primitive surviving subgroup and
its limiting homomorphism give exactly $\Gamma_\infty$
(\hyperref[push:src:D.3.1]{\ref*{push:src:D.3.1}}).

Choosing successively separated
scales realizes every primitive subgroup and limiting
homomorphism.  Pontryagin--Chabauty duality converts their dual
graphs to the stated real-torus additive quotients
(\hyperref[push:src:D.3.1]{\ref*{push:src:D.3.1}}).

At fixed boundary parameter,
irrational root rays make all noncentral dual labels escape.
The surviving rational label is
$\operatorname{lcm}(2,n)\Re\xi$; its circle-valued function
separates precisely the asserted classes.  Collapsing those
classes proves the universal Hausdorff-reflection property
(\hyperref[push:src:D.2.3]{\ref*{push:src:D.2.3}}).

main_theorems.title: The cotangent term and the exact generic-vanishing criterion
main_theorems.label: series:II:A

steps.claim_tex:
The conormal map is injective at
each generic smooth point of the reduced hypersurface. Its inverse
image of cotangent torsion gives the two exact sequences, and their
cohomology identifies the ambient section space with the stated
connecting-map kernel
(\hyperref[cdp:st:A.1.1]{\ref*{cdp:st:A.1.1}}).

The node has normalization
$u\mapsto(u^2-1,u(u^2-1))$ and identifies $u=1,-1$. Its gluing-line
complex is $\C\xrightarrow{1-\lambda}\C$, while the inverse
image of torsion is the pushforward of the trivial normalization
line. Taking the product with $\PP^1$ gives the asserted
counterexample dimensions
(\hyperref[cdp:st:B1]{\ref*{cdp:st:B1}}).

Transgression gives unitary
infinite-order twists on every fibre support; the canonical
injection of twisted torsion-free forms into local-system
cohomology gives their vanishing
(\hyperref[cdp:st:A.4.7]{\ref*{cdp:st:A.4.7}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:A.4.9]{\ref*{cdp:st:A.4.9}}).

Full Cartier filtrations reduce
generic ambient vanishing to irreducible nonnormal supports.
Normalization Picard pullback determines persistence of their
conductor section, yielding exactly the displayed global
criterion (\hyperref[cdp:st:C4f]{\ref*{cdp:st:C4f}}).

The Poincar\'e transform and
cohomology of $\OO_{\PP^1}(-2)$ produce the length-one higher
direct image. Stabilization of the finite-dimensional section
spaces and the associated-component calculation give the exact
divisor-twisting statement
(\hyperref[cdp:st:E12]{\ref*{cdp:st:E12}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:E17]{\ref*{cdp:st:E17}}).

main_theorems.title: Component count and the smooth general fibre
main_theorems.label: series:II:B

steps.claim_tex:
Lifts of the free generators of
$\pi_1(C\setminus\Delta)$ split the punctured bundle group.
Its abelianization is $\Z^{2g+s-1}\oplus H_1(F,\Z)_{\pi_1}$;
the compact-support sequence then gives the component count and
integral freeness (\hyperref[cdp:st:D.1.2]{\ref*{cdp:st:D.1.2}}).

Fibre adjunction and divisor
Riemann--Roch give the displayed Chern and coherent-Euler
identities. Surface classification supplies the finite necessary
list (\hyperref[cdp:st:C.3.1]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.3.1}}).

The explicit surface-group and
monodromy comparisons exclude the bielliptic, Kodaira and Inoue
entries; relative algebraic reduction forces the surviving Hopf
fibre to have algebraic dimension zero
(\hyperref[cdp:st:C.3.7]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.3.7}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:C.3.8]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.3.8}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:C.3.9]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.3.9}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:C.3.10]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.3.10}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:C.3.12]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.3.12}}).

The quotient and filling maps
produce the surviving primary and secondary Hopf types and a fixed
abelian general fibre (\hyperref[cdp:st:C.3.6]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.3.6}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:D.2.7]{\ref*{cdp:st:D.2.7}}).

main_theorems.title: The sign for every degeneration and its equality criterion
main_theorems.label: series:II:C

steps.claim_tex:
Connected-fibre Leray makes the
base rational. Finite-character support comparison and local
conductor maps give the irreducible values zero and two and their
normalization descriptions; the normal-crossing calculation gives
the triple-point count
(\hyperref[night:P4.58]{\ref*{night:P4.58}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:C.2.MH.2]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.2.MH.2}}).

An adjacent component pulls back
to a nonzero effective divisor with rational Chern class zero.
The surface and Picard comparisons leave the Hopf, non-K\"ahler
elliptic and Enoki possibilities and then exclude the Enoki
interfaces through the explicit local vanishing sphere
(\hyperref[cdp:st:C.2.INT.1]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.2.INT.1}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:C.2.INT.2]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.2.INT.2}}).

Coherent conductor duality, curve
normalization and exact blowup counts give nonnegative summands
for every surviving reducible support. Equality forces the stated
minimal normalizations and unramified elliptic conductor maps
(\hyperref[cdp:st:C.2.INT.3]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.2.INT.3}}).

Euler additivity gives
$e(Y)=\sum_b e(S_b)$. The nondegenerate skew pairing on $H^3$
and $e(Y)=2-b_3(Y)$ give the two values and the global equality
criterion (\hyperref[cdp:st:C.2.G.1]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.2.G.1}}).

For identity monodromy, a
persistent positive-index obstruction has a fixed irreducible
support. The Gauduchon degree and conductor calculation makes
its normalization geometric genus zero; vertical resolution
preserves that property on all components. The logarithmic
period obstruction contradicts identity monodromy, giving
$c_3(Y)\le0$ and hence equality
(\hyperref[cdp:st:D.2.3]{\ref*{cdp:st:D.2.3}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:D.2.5]{\ref*{cdp:st:D.2.5}}).

The retained three-piece
holomorphic filling and its integral Mayer--Vietoris maps give
$H_1=H_2=0$ and Euler number zero
(\hyperref[cdp:st:D.2.7]{\ref*{cdp:st:D.2.7}}).

main_theorems.title: Local parity and prescribed Euler numbers
main_theorems.label: series:II:D

steps.claim_tex:
A full fibre tube $U$ retracts
onto the support, and its boundary $M$ is the nearby torus mapping
torus. Pair duality gives
$e(U)\equiv b_0(M)+b_1(M)+b_2(M)$ modulo two
(\hyperref[cdp:st:C.2.UN.1]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.2.UN.1}}).

Wang identifies that parity with
$\dim\ker(\Lambda^2T-I)$. The wedge pairing and Cayley transform
make this dimension even for every orientation-preserving torus
monodromy (\hyperref[cdp:st:C.2.UN.1]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.2.UN.1}}).

Replacing a smooth codimension-$r$
centre by its exceptional projective bundle changes support Euler
number by $(r-1)e(C)$. A point adds two; a plane quartic after a
point blowup gives net change minus two. Iteration gives every
prescribed value and cofinal zero-Euler models
(\hyperref[cdp:st:C.2.UN.4]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.2.UN.4}}).

Strict transforms are
bimeromorphic on normalization resolutions and preserve their
base-function valuations. Every new exceptional surface is
explicitly ruled or rational, proving the multiset assertion
(\hyperref[cdp:st:C.2.UN.14]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.2.UN.14}}).

The genus-two curve in the
projective product family and disjoint point blowups realize all
values $2(m-k)$ in compact projective threefolds
(\hyperref[cdp:st:C.2.UN.2]{\ref*{cdp:st:C.2.UN.2}}).

main_theorems.title: Twisted tangent cohomology of the standard family
main_theorems.label: series:II:E

steps.claim_tex:
The stabilizer characters on the
root curve give the integral degrees $d(n)$, with direct-image
summands $d(n)$, $d(n-1)$, $d(n+2)$ and $d(n+6)$ and the
specified finite root contribution
(\hyperref[cdp:st:C5b]{\ref*{cdp:st:C5b}}).

Cohomology of each line on
$\PP^1$ gives the four displayed dimensions. The actual cusp
map has the stated rank locus, including its zero value at
$n=-1$ (\hyperref[cdp:st:C5b]{\ref*{cdp:st:C5b}}).

The exact translation-character
complex is acyclic off resonance. At a regular resonance its
local modules have two degree-one generators and a length-two
degree-two generator; finite-root characters give
$\ell_1,\ell_2$ (\hyperref[cdp:st:C5c]{\ref*{cdp:st:C5c}}).

Properness of the direct-image
support makes the regular resonance set finite. The cusp adds
one reduced degree-two skyscraper and its nonzero map to the
normalization target. Leray gives $(0,J_z,1+J_z,0)$
(\hyperref[cdp:st:C5c]{\ref*{cdp:st:C5c}}).

The identity-induced degree-six
isogeny gives the symmetric period matrix. The theta heat equation
and the eta derivative retain the Weierstrass term in the exact
determinant; the original branch equation then gives its stated
rank locus (\hyperref[cdp:st:E8]{\ref*{cdp:st:E8}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:E18]{\ref*{cdp:st:E18}}).

main_theorems.title: Fibration retention and deformation spaces
main_theorems.label: series:II:F

steps.claim_tex:
At a smooth fibre the boundary
map sends $a\eta_1+b\eta_2$ to
$(bu_1-au_2)\otimes\eta_1\wedge\eta_2$. Rank two makes it
injective and kills the infinitesimal map obstruction over
$\PP^1$ (\hyperref[cdp:st:E5]{\ref*{cdp:st:E5}}).

The same cup-product comparison
at every Artin order, followed by the relative graph construction,
gives the extending map over the analytic germ, with its
connected torus fibres and stated algebraic dimension
(\hyperref[cdp:st:E6]{\ref*{cdp:st:E6}}).

Root-curve tangent cohomology
and the actual two-parameter period sections give the two smooth
surface germs and their tuples
(\hyperref[cdp:st:E13]{\ref*{cdp:st:E13}},
\hyperref[cdp:st:E14]{\ref*{cdp:st:E14}}).

Admissible comb period sections
realize every tangent direction while retaining affine attachments.
Their tangent isomorphism makes the Kuranishi ideal zero and gives
the displayed comb dimensions
(\hyperref[cdp:st:E15]{\ref*{cdp:st:E15}}).

Disc propagation and finite
curve projections make the fixed ordered-pair locus open and
closed in a connected reduced analytic base. This gives
separation through arbitrary finite deformation chains
(\hyperref[push:src:E.2.23]{\ref*{push:src:E.2.23}}).

The Kuranishi retraction transports
that separation to the $C^\infty$ space of integrable structures
and to the indicated diffeomorphism quotients
(\hyperref[push:src:E.2.24]{\ref*{push:src:E.2.24}}).

main_theorems.title: The Liu--Rollenske covering parameter
main_theorems.label: series:II:G

steps.claim_tex:
The exact scalar is $\alpha=cu$
with fixed $c\ne0$. Setting $\tau=\log(cu)/(2\pi i)$ gives
the central lattice generated by $(2,0),(1+i,0),(1,1/2),(0,\tau)$
and affine fourth-root action
$(z,\eta)\mapsto(-iz,\eta+\tau/4+\kappa)$, where
$4\kappa\in\Z$ (\hyperref[ii:LR:covering]{\ref*{ii:LR:covering}}).

Projection to $\eta$ is the
Albanese map with period lattice
$\tfrac12\Z+(\tau/4+\kappa)\Z$. One $u$-turn sends its
Tate parameter $Q$ to $-Q$; $Q(j(Q)-j(-Q))$ tends to two,
excluding a fibre biholomorphism
(\hyperref[ii:LR:covering]{\ref*{ii:LR:covering}}).

Ambient $H^2(Y,\R)=0$ makes
every effective divisor vertical. Meromorphic functions therefore
descend through the torus fibration; any endpoint biholomorphism
preserves its unique multiplicity-four fibre. The previous step
excludes every one-turn endpoint
(\hyperref[ii:LR:covering]{\ref*{ii:LR:covering}}).

The lifted translation by the
marked source section, its rational square root and cap
commutators give the two-turn endpoint map. Its exact two-step
norm equals the prescribed one-gamma gluing, including the cusp
multiplier. The resulting free quotient has parameter
$w=r^2$ and $u=w^2$
(\hyperref[ii:LR:covering]{\ref*{ii:LR:covering}}).

main_theorems.title: The prescribed quotient and relative extensions
main_theorems.label: series:III:A

steps.claim_tex:
Use the primitive circle quotient and its explicit period
comparison from Paper~I.  The comparison preserves the signed primitive
covector, so the quotient and its boundary meridian are fixed maps.

The cusp target is the solid torus supplied by the local quotient
construction.  Its higher homotopy group in degree six is zero, which
gives the relative uniqueness within this prescribed target.

Choose a closed six-ball in the interior of the cusp
neighbourhood.  Collapse its boundary to obtain the relative pinch
$X\to X\vee S^6$, equal to the identity off the ball.

Compose the first summand with $e$ and the second with a
representative of $\alpha\in\pi_6(S^3)$.  The resulting map agrees
with $e$ on the exterior and represents $[e]+\alpha$.
This proves the exact scope of the extension assertion.

main_theorems.title: The quotient and algebraic-reduction homotopy classes
main_theorems.label: series:III:B

steps.claim_tex:
Express the framing difference on the regular four-torus.
Its degree-one obstruction is the common invariant covector $\gamma$
modulo two.  Restriction to $\ker\gamma$ therefore lifts this
comparison to $\operatorname{Spin}$.

Twice the remaining degree-three obstruction is the restriction
of the common invariant class dual to the invariant vector $d$.
Since $d\in\ker\gamma$, this restriction is zero.  The integral
third cohomology of the three-torus is torsion-free, so the obstruction
itself is zero.

Pontryagin--Thom now represents $e$ by the Lie-framed
three-torus.  The periodic flat Dirac operator has paired nonzero
spectrum and a two-dimensional kernel.  The normalization in
\cite[Theorem~4.14, p.~423]{mapsAPS2} gives real $e$-invariant $1/2$.

Toda's stabilization calculation identifies the injected
$\pi_6(S^3)$ with the subgroup generated by $2\nu$ in the stable
three-stem.  The class with this invariant is $6\nu'$, also the
displayed composite of the three Hopf maps
\cite[Theorem~4.1 and Corollaries~4.2--4.3]{mapsToda52}.

In the two multiplicative coordinates, the normalized power map
is $P_{3,4}(z_1,z_2)=(z_1^3,z_2^4)/\|(z_1^3,z_2^4)\|$.
A regular value has twelve positively oriented inverse images, so its
degree is twelve.

The marked quotient construction gives the equality of maps
$f=H\circ P_{3,4}\circ e$, where $H:S^3\to S^2$ is the Hopf
map and $\PP^1$ is identified with $S^2$ by the stated orientation.

The degree-twelve self-map acts by multiplication by twelve on
$\pi_6(S^3)=\Z/12$.  Thus $P_{3,4}\circ e$ is null-homotopic;
postcomposition with $H$ gives the required null-homotopy of $f$.
The body also gives the normalized-section homotopy directly.

main_theorems.title: The retained-angle cusp map and finite cell model
main_theorems.label: series:III:C

steps.claim_tex:
Define the map in the triple-point chart using the retained
angle and the two radial coordinates.  Keep the bounded period
correction when differentiating the normal frame.

The resulting frame differs from the product frame by
$\operatorname{diag}(e^{-i(a+b)},e^{ia},e^{ib})$ in
$\operatorname{SU}(3)$.  The displayed two $\operatorname{SU}(2)$
factor homotopies contract this comparison.

The inverse-image torus therefore has its Lie framing.  Its
spin quadratic form has Arf invariant one, so its Pontryagin--Thom
class is the nonzero $\eta_4\eta_5$.

Two allowed real-period lifts agree on the exterior collar;
their straight-line interpolation gives a relative homotopy.
The core-collapse comparison factors through the specified
$S^3\vee S^2$ cofiber, with the map using its $S^3$ summand.
These are the explicit comparisons among the cusp maps.

Construct the regular mapping-cylinder bundle using the actual
integral monodromies.  In every finite affine cap retain the drift
from the logarithmic translation; it is part of the attaching map. In the cusp write the seam map as
$[a,b,\theta]\mapsto[a,b-\theta(B_0a-v(a))]$.
The frozen-period comparison is an explicit logarithmic-coordinate
homeomorphism and agrees with the prescribed boundary markings.

The positive quotient has interior $T^2\times(0,1)$ and the
two marked boundary tori.  Its incompressible boundary and the
induced fundamental-group isomorphism meet Waldhausen's
boundary-fixed product criterion
\cite[Theorem~6.1, p.~77]{mapsWaldhausen68}. Triangulate these marked pieces and their common faces.  The
resulting mapping-cylinder cells have the displayed counts, and
their alternating sum is two.

Van Kampen gives the relations $x^3=x^4=1$.  The primitive
finite pullback lattices and the two cusp sweeps give unimodular
integral attachments, so $H_1=H_2=0$.  Duality, the Euler number,
Hurewicz and Whitehead finish the sphere identification.

main_theorems.title: The relative Kummer cover and its global completion
main_theorems.label: series:III:D

steps.claim_tex:
On the $N$th root of the base use the actual period
$C(v^N)/N$.  The monomial maps and their lattice inclusions
separate the absolute degree-$N^3$ map from its relative
degree-$N^2$ map.

Across adjacent unimodular triangles, smoothness imposes the
displayed divisibility relations on primitive ray indices.
The reverse relations force equality, so a smooth full-fan cover
must use the scalar toric sublattice $n\Z^3$.

Continue the prescribed local Kummer lattice by the marked
order-four monodromy.  Its toric intersection is
$\Z w\oplus N\Z d$.  Its primitive ray indices violate that
scalar condition for $N>1$.

The explicit word
$A_2^2A_1A_2^2A_1^{-1}$ also produces $N^2$ distinct based
lattices; their residues are exhibited in the body.  The finite
semidirect quotient supplies a global cover with the required
local lattice.

Its normal monomial completion has a free basis indexed by
fractional exponents in a half-open fundamental box.  This proves
finite flatness of that normal completion while recording the
smoothness obstruction above.

main_theorems.title: The cyclic universal covers
main_theorems.label: series:III:E

steps.claim_tex:
The connected cusp cover has $d$ components in its periodic
normalization.  Its Laurent relation matrix reduces integrally
to $\operatorname{diag}(1,t-1,t-1,0)$.

The nontrivial deck characters make the regular torus Koszul
complex acyclic.  The primitive finite-cap degree-two pullbacks
and the cusp sweep with coefficient $d$ determine the integral
groups, including their torsion.

The $d$ cusp divisors give classes $x_i$ with
$\sum x_i=0$ and
$x_ix_j=(\mathbf1_{j=i+1}+\mathbf1_{j=i-1}-2\mathbf1_{j=i})\kappa$,
where $\kappa$ generates the degree-four torsion.

For the finite-coefficient class $u$ the body computes
$\langle ux_ix_j,[M_d]\rangle$ by the same cyclic matrix,
$\langle u^2x_i,[M_d]\rangle=-12$, and
$\langle u^3,[M_d]\rangle=0$ modulo $d$.  The support-function
restriction has square $-12$, which fixes the second value.

Transfer kills the integral pullback in degree four, so
$c_2=p_1=0$.  Multiplication by four is injective on
$\Z^{d-1}\oplus\Z/d$, giving zero refined Pontryagin class.
The full $H_6(K(H_2,2))$ calculation shows that these evaluations
specify the remaining invariant; Zhubr's classification applies
to the already constructed covers.

Euler multiplicativity gives $\chi=2d$.  A connected sum of
$g$ copies of $S^3\times S^3$ has Euler number $2-2g$; for
$d>1$ the equality would require $g=1-d<0$.  This supplies the
numerical obstruction to that proposed connected-sum type.

main_theorems.title: The marked elliptic profiles and their integral outputs
main_theorems.label: series:III:F

steps.claim_tex:
Fix the initial section pair, the component on which the
linearization vanishes, the marked filling and every affine
logarithmic vector.  The profile is the elliptic-fibre configuration;
a pattern is the entire marked initial row, with its stated
arithmetic conditions.

Compute the primitive specialization lattices and the actual
normal-circle-torus maps.  Regular-fibre restriction is carried
through the boundary and Gysin maps before the finite-coefficient
classes are used.  Their integral cokernels retain all torsion.

The all-order calculations for the original, III-star,
Liu--Rollenske and Wang families give their explicit determinant
or normal-torus matrices.  The additive and multiplicative local
calculations close the remaining profiles; the complete table in
\cref{maps:src:D.2.28} records every pattern.

In the simply connected residual cases retain the spin
characteristic class, Zhubr's refined class and the full
fundamental-class image.  The conic surgery and the marked
$Z_{c,\epsilon}$ surgeries give explicit representatives of the
types in \cref{maps:src:D.2.44}, \cref{maps:src:D.2.45}.

For a period sublattice of the cusp, intersect the component
restrictions on each degree-six del Pezzo normalization.  Keep
loops, repeated edges and repeated vertices in this calculation;
the complete trilinear expression is
\cref{maps:src:D.2.47}.

In the simply connected weight-$d$ sector the Seifert
determinant is $P=\pm1$.  The full invariant includes the
Pontryagin square modulo $d\gcd(d,2)$ and the third power
modulo $d\gcd(d,3)$, with evaluations $-12$ and $0$.
Together with the cyclic divisor matrix and refined class zero,
these give the single type $M_d$ in \cref{maps:src:D.2.48}.

For a free OS49 cap $(m,n,d)=(3k,n,d)$ with $n\ne0$,
put $g=\gcd(3k,n,3d)$.  The exact primitive Gysin lattice has
Smith invariants $g,|n|$, giving
$H_2=H_3=\Z/|n|\oplus\Z/g$ with $g\in\{1,3\}$.
For example $(9,3,1)$ gives $(\Z/3)^2$.
The zero-$n$ calculation and the precise freeness conditions are
retained in \cref{night:P3F.33}, \cref{night:P3F.34}.

main_theorems.title: The conifold transition
main_theorems.label: series:III:G

steps.claim_tex:
Start with the marked elliptic surface and the line
$M=\OO(P-O)$.  Move the linearization as $\phi_s=\phi_0-s\phi_1$,
using its exact annular identification on the common exterior.

Near the collision the equation is
$xy=u(zv-s)$.  At $s=0$ this is the ordinary double point;
its small resolution has exceptional normal bundle
$\OO(-1)\oplus\OO(-1)$.  The root caps remain in the same
proper family because the collars were chosen uniformly.

On real manifolds the transition replaces $S^2\times D^4$
by $D^3\times S^3$.  General position makes the complement
simply connected; Alexander duality and the two primitive boundary
maps give $H_3=\Z^2$ and $H_2=H_4=0$.

The spin Wall invariant has the standard rank-two skew form
and zero normal invariant.  The classification, together with
$\Theta_6=0$, identifies the smoothing with $S^3\times S^3$.

The root canonical formula and the varying periods give
algebraic dimension one.  The formal cohomology of the exceptional
curve transports the stated structure-sheaf cohomology across the
small resolution.  The comparison with the published CDP quotient
uses its actual algebraic-reduction fibres in
\cref{maps:src:D.3.4}.

main_theorems.title: The physical transfer and the reference return
main_theorems.label: series:IV:A

\[
 [\Phi]=A_M:=\frac{4k_M-\ell_M}{24}\pmod{28},\qquad
 \mu(\Sigma_\Phi)=A_M/28\pmod{\mathbb Z}.
\]
The global inverse-line map $D(v)(v)=1$, with
$D(cv)=c^{-1}D(v)$, gives
$(k_U,\ell_U,A_U)=-(k_M,\ell_M,A_M)$ on the same oriented quotient.
Its spinor and cap maps identify the physical transfer with
$-\Sigma_{F^{-1}}=\Sigma_F$. In the coordinates used by
\cref{night:P3F.22}, the two normalizing inputs
$(k,\ell)(a)=(1,4)$ and $(k,\ell)(b)=(8,8)$ give
$\mu(\lambda(a))=0$ and $\mu(\lambda(b))=1/28$.

For the canonical whole-zero reference pages of
\cref{night:P3K.26,night:P3K.28,iv:correction:P3K.32}, retain their
actual source, root caps, signed norm equation and ordinary framing.
If the marked section has height $h(G)=1/d$, the line point is $aG$,
the product of the retained root orders is $M_0$, and

\[
 (k_M,\ell_M)=(3H,24\chi),\quad A_M=H/2-\chi,
 \quad(m_{\rm native},n_{\rm native})=(6\chi,3H-6\chi).
\]
These statements use the fixed reference cusp fan and its full page
comparison. For the coprime $(3K,4L)$ sphere construction,

$4Ln_0+3Kn_1=\pm1$, the reference return is zero with the reference
fan, lattice basis and collar maps of \cref{night:P3F.10}.

and the two page characteristic terms then cancel on the reference fan.

the complete source and convention checks are recorded at

main_theorems.title: Primitive generators, the source catalogue and the fixed-edge flop
main_theorems.label: series:IV:B

\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
d&\text{profiles}\\\hline

\end{array}
\]
Use $M=\mathcal O([dG]-[O])$, translation by $-G$, a simple
whole-fibre zero at a chosen $I_1$, the standard vertical-edge cusp

Their primitive positive scalar loops have physical pair $(3d,24)$
and integer $d/2-1$, namely $3,6,9,14$.

$g=R^3+\tfrac32tR+\tfrac38$ in

families, the native right integer is $6A_M$, and the directed flop
has class $7A_M$. Thus the four primitive groups give

The retained broader catalogue has sixteen profiles, twenty-six source

The other thirty branches retain those equations, their coprimality
conditions and their full cap maps; their canonical reference integer

main_theorems.title: Scalar returns on every ordered cusp fan
main_theorems.label: series:IV:C
main_theorems.statement_tex:
Retain one of the actual fixed-source, whole-zero $I_1$ sphere families
of \cref{night:P3K.26,night:P3K.28,iv:correction:P3K.32}, with
its Cartier line, source translation, finite characters, full annular

\[
 J=M_0/c_{\rm cov},\quad \widehat H=H/c_{\rm cov},\quad
 \widehat\chi=\chi/c_{\rm cov}.
\]
Every $T(P)$ has an actual integer return computed by the terminating
canonical fan word and target-prism algorithm of
\cref{night:P3K.73}. Its vertical value is
\[
 A(T_j)=\widehat H/2-\widehat\chi-Jj(j-1)/2.
\]
At each directed native step the actual doubled ordinary variation
$V$ and derivative $\delta$ give the single-loop addition

$w_h=e^{-\pi i c/(KL)}=r^6$ and

 y^2=x^3-3t^3(t-1)x+2t^4(t-1)(t-\tfrac12),\quad G=(t^2,t^2),
\]

The constructed shortest scalar winding is $kh$, with

main_theorems.title: The marked source loops and their exact parameter degrees
main_theorems.label: series:IV:D

 Y^2=X^3+(1-2v)X^2+TX+v^2,\quad G=(0,v),\quad q=T-(v^2-2v),

contracting scalar and endpoint. The terminating algorithm of
\cref{night:P3K.90} computes every basis fan. On $T_j$ put
\[
 \mu_0=2-a+6pk,\qquad
 A_j=2b\binom{j+1}{3}+(3-b)\binom{j+1}{2}
       +k(a-1)(3p-1)-km\binom j2.
\]
Its physical pair is $(\mu_0+6A_j,4\mu_0)$ and return is $A_j$.

 y^2=x^3+(-2+3\epsilon^2)x^2+tx+\epsilon^2(1-\epsilon^2)^2,
 \quad G=(0,\epsilon(1-\epsilon^2)),
\]
and selected height $q_*=t-(1-\epsilon^2)(1-3\epsilon^2)$,
with the full source/root closing of \cref{night:P3K.92}.

\[
 I_a(P)=1-a-3(a-1)(S(P)-1)
        -\frac{2a+1}{4}(S(P)-1)(S(P)-3)\pmod{28}.
\]
The exact images are
$\{0,6,8,10,14,20,22,24\}$ for $a=1$ and
$\{5,7,9,13,19,21,23,27\}$ for $a=2$.
With $J_{\rm ref}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)$, its actual boundary
relation is $I_a(P)=-Z_a(P)-Z_a(J_{\rm ref}P)-C(P)$, where

main_theorems.title: The resolved transverse elliptic fibre product

steps.claim_tex:

threefold fibration.  The integral matrices $A,B$ give the actual

give $(h^{0,q})=(1,1,0,0,0)$; the explicit meromorphic product
comparison gives algebraic dimension two.

$b_1$ and $h^{0,1}$.  Here $b_1=0$ and $h^{0,1}=1$, contradicting
the K\"ahler equality $b_1=2h^{0,1}$.  This proves the stated
exclusion through these invariants.

The universal Todd and Pontryagin formulas give

positive definite unimodular of rank two, hence has the displayed
form.  The body records the precise scope of each cited formula.

main_theorems.title: The integral rank-six construction
main_theorems.label: series:V:B

steps.claim_tex:
The matrices $M_1=A^t$, $M_2=B^t$ have orders five and four, and
  $N=(M_1M_2)^{-1}-I$ has square zero and primitive image of rank three.
  The displayed unimodular marking takes $N$ to
  $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&I_3\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$;
  the invariant covector $\ell(x)=x_0$ proves freeness of every
  nonidentity affine power
  (\cref{maps:src:F.2.5}, \cref{night:P1.1}).

The cusp and finite quotient charts glue to a closed smooth
  manifold.  Killing the invariant normal closure of the cusp angular lattice
  leaves the central fibre generator $h$ and the relations $5a=h$, $4b=-h$, $a+b=0$;
  their integral relation matrix is unimodular, so the fundamental
  group vanishes (\cref{maps:src:F.2.5}, \cref{night:P1.10}).

Unimodular coordinates identify the finite core monodromies
  with a five-cycle and a four-cycle plus a sign.  Their actual
  covering maps induce invariant vertical cochains and norm sums
  on the prism cochains.  Together with the primitive cusp collapse,
  these maps give the displayed integral sheaf complex; its signed
  orbit bases and determinant minors give the sheaf groups
  (\cref{maps:src:F.2.6}, items~1--4; \cref{night:P1.11}).

For the order-four core and normal loops $g,h$, the fibre and
  transverse loops are $v=g^4h^{-1}$ and $t=g$; their integral
  basis matrix has determinant one.  A torsion representative $w$
  pulls back to $(Nw,w)=(0,w)$ in these two directions.
  Thus its transgression is $\pm[w]$.  The printed modulo-two
  rows detect all three nonzero global classes
  (\cref{maps:src:F.2.6}, item~5;
  \cref{mapsaudit:order-four-torsion-transgression}).

The three torsion differentials are isomorphisms onto
  $\mathbb Z/2$.  On the cusp term $\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2$,
  the remaining kernel is generated by $(1,\epsilon)$, where
  $\epsilon$ is the image of its free generator.
  The Leray filtration therefore gives $H^3=0$ and
  $H^4=\mathbb Z^4$.  Universal coefficients, duality and
  Hurewicz give the asserted free homology and three-connectivity
  (\cref{maps:src:F.2.6}, item~6; \cref{night:P1.12}).

The compatible almost complex structure has $c_1=c_3=0$.
  Todd integrality and the signature bound $|\sigma|\leq4$ force
  $c_2^2=2$, $p_1^2=8$, $p_2=14$ and $\sigma=2$.
  Its unimodular middle lattice is consequently the odd form
  $I_{3,1}$ (\cref{night:P1.13}).

main_theorems.title: The genus-two period construction
main_theorems.label: series:V:C

steps.claim_tex:
The pencil has one node at $\lambda_*=-256/3125$ and good
  reductions after root orders eight and five.  Its Hodge bundle on
  that root curve is $T^3\oplus T$, with
  $T=\mathcal O((2/5)[\infty]-(3/8)[0])$ and
  $\deg T=1/40$ (\cref{night:P1.4}).

In the exterior-square lattice, projection induces
  $j:\omega^\perp\to(\bigwedge^2\mathbb Z^4)/\mathbb Z\omega$
  with Smith factors $(1,1,1,1,2)$.  This exact index-two map identifies
  the rational systems, and the quotient is the dual of the primitive
  integral lattice.  The lower five-dimensional blocks of the given
  rank-six tuple are the quotient blocks under this map
  (\cref{night:P1.2}).

Put $P=p(\ell_0\wedge\mathcal H_{\mathrm{dR}})$, where
  $\ell_0=\langle dx/y\rangle$ and $p$ is projection modulo $\omega$.
  The wedge map has rank three and its image meets $\mathbb C\omega$
  trivially: a decomposable two-vector has square zero, whereas
  $\omega^2\ne0$.  This proves the required rank before a lift is
  chosen (\cref{night:P1.5}, \cref{maps:src:F.3.5}).

The orbifold extension over $P$ splits because
  $H^1(P^*)=0$, as computed from its two line-bundle extensions and
  their integral floor degrees.  A chosen splitting $\sigma$ and
  the canonical functional $\alpha:P\to\mathcal O$ give
  $F_\xi=(\sigma+\xi\alpha e)P$
  (\cref{maps:src:F.3.5}, \cref{night:P1.7}).

On the real line $P\cap\overline P$, choose $n$ with
  $\alpha(n)=1$ and write
  $\sigma(n)-\overline{\sigma(n)}=2ih e$.
  Then $F_\xi\cap\overline{F_\xi}=0$ exactly when
  $h+\operatorname{Im}\xi\ne0$.  At the cusp the period matrix is
  $Z=(\log q)/(2\pi i)I_3+C(q)$, with $C$ holomorphic and bounded;
  hence $h\to+\infty$ and a sufficiently large imaginary shift
  works on the whole completed base
  (\cref{maps:src:F.3.6}, \cref{night:P1.8}).

main_theorems.title: The oriented diffeomorphism type
main_theorems.label: series:V:D

steps.claim_tex:
The lifted periods commute with the finite root actions and
  have the prescribed bounded cusp correction, so the same quotient
  and toroidal charts are holomorphic and proper.  Their collar
  identifications are the marked maps used in the smooth construction
  (\cref{maps:src:F.3.7}, \cref{night:P1.9}).

The preceding integral calculation gives the intersection
  lattice $I_{3,1}$.  The spin characteristic vector $p_1/2$ has
  square two, by the Chern-number calculation
  (\cref{night:P1.13}).

In an odd diagonal basis write its coordinates, after sign
  changes, as positive odd integers $(a,b,c,d)$.  A reflection in
  $(1,1,1,1)$ replaces $d$ by $2d-a-b-c$, whose absolute value is
  smaller when $d>1$.  Iteration terminates at $(1,1,1,1)$, proving
  an isometry of the lattice together with its characteristic vector
  (\cref{maps:src:F.4.1}).

In the quaternionic clutching coordinates, the actual map is
  $(a,b)\mapsto(e,p_1/2)=(a-b,a+b)$, with inverse
  $((e+p_1/2)/2,(p_1/2-e)/2)$.  Thus the pairing and characteristic
  vector determine the normal datum; the Poincar\'e-duality map
  transports it with the middle lattice isometry
  (\cref{maps:src:F.4.1}).

Each quaternionic projective-plane summand has $p_1=2u$.
  The oriented connected-sum pairing and characteristic vector are
  therefore the same pair $\bigl(I_{3,1},(1,1,1,1)\bigr)$.
  Wall's stated extended-form classification gives the oriented
  diffeomorphism up to a homotopy eight-sphere
  (\cref{maps:src:F.4.1}).

Kramer--Stolz's Theorem A absorbs that sphere in one positive
  $\mathbb{HP}^2$ summand.  Its diffeomorphism has degree $+1$ because
  the square of a middle generator evaluates to $1$ on both sides.
  Oriented connected-sum maps therefore give the required oriented
  diffeomorphism of the full fourfold
  (\cref{maps:src:F.4.1}).

main_theorems.title: The exact family and its two ends
main_theorems.label: series:V:E

steps.claim_tex:
The real coordinate and marked deck maps preserve the normalized
  height. The infinity-root rotation fixes its differential at zero;
  an invertible real system and the positive Hessian prove a strict
  local minimum. Convergent root and cusp series and exact collar
  continuation enclose all 1600 leaves of the closed covers above
  that value. The actual cusp graph has a positive determinant on
  the remaining inner disc and tends to positive height without
  bound. These maps prove the unique global minimum and identify
  the transversality domain exactly with $\mathcal U$
  (\cref{night:P1.18}, proof, items 1--7).

On the effective root curve of orders five and four put
  $L=\mathcal O((4/5)[\infty]-(3/4)[0])$.  The direct images are
  $R^qh_*\mathcal O=\bigwedge^q
  (\mathcal O\oplus L^{-1}\oplus L^{-2})$, and
  $K_M=h^*L^{-6}$.  The toric normalization complex proves the
  exterior-algebra assertion at the cusp, and the root-chart
  invariant cohomology proves it at the finite fibres
  (\cref{night:P1A.1}).

The logarithmic cotangent sequence and its explicit residue
  matrices give the Hodge table below.  Serre duality applied to
  the twisted logarithmic and residue sequences gives
  $h^q(T_M)=(1,1,1,2,0)$.  The normal tangent map and the actual
  period lift give a nonzero Kodaira--Spencer class; the local
  analytic-ring comparison makes the Kuranishi germ smooth of
  dimension one (\cref{night:P1A.2}, \cref{night:P1A.3}).

Restriction of a horizontal divisor to a regular torus fibre
  gives an invariant alternating class.  The computed invariant
  space is zero, while positive pairing with a torus Kähler form
  rules out a nonzero effective divisor of zero class.  Thus the
  meromorphic field is the base field $\mathbb C(\lambda)$.
  Every isomorphism therefore preserves the base and its three
  distinguished values.  The simultaneous linear centralizer is
  $\mathbb Q I$; the order-five affine norm excludes its negative
  integral unit.  The translation sheaf has identity component
  $\mathbb C$ and an integral parabolic quotient $\mathbb Z/2$,
  represented by the displayed half-period, proving the
  automorphism group and equality of parameters for isomorphic
  members (\cref{night:P1A.4}).

The two integral anti-intertwiners are $\pm R$.  One is excluded
  by the finite cap norm.  For the other, the actual based cusp
  correction acts on rays by $-P$, and takes $e_2$ to $(0,-1,1)$,
  outside the component's rays $\pm(\{0,1\}^3\setminus\{0\})$.
  The corresponding monomial map contracts a divisor, contradicting
  a biholomorphism (\cref{night:P1.17}).

A proposed proper Hausdorff filling across a boundary point of
  a full parameter disc recovers the marked base from the moving
  pencil of $K_M^{-4}$, whose two sections have ratio $\lambda$.
  Closed relative forms give actual torus fibres outside a proper
  analytic subset.  Their marked periods continue as $F_\xi$,
  while the real hypersurface $h_b+\operatorname{Im}\xi=0$
  cannot be contained in that analytic subset.  A torus fibre
  there violates real transversality (\cref{night:P1A.5}).  For a family on a punctured disc whose
  fibres belong to $\mathcal U$, the unique classifying map is
  holomorphic; its Cayley transform extends and the maximum principle
  keeps its limit inside $\mathcal U$.  After the explicit degree-two
  removal of the finite torsor, that family has a smooth filling
  (\cref{night:P1A.6}).

steps.claim_tex:
Primitive square-zero cusp matrices have the explicit integral
  normal form and centralizer
  $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}P&Q\\0&P\end{smallmatrix}\right)$.
  Eigenvalue one is necessary for a free affine lift, leaving the
  finite cyclotomic list and its complex-compatibility filter
  (\cref{maps:src:F.2.1}, \cref{maps:src:F.2.2}).

The rational intertwiner algebra, its radical and its
  semisimple quotient reduce the simultaneous integral-conjugacy
  problem to the cited lattice-isomorphism algorithm in its verified
  hypothesis.  Searching by height and lexicographic order terminates
  by the input height, yielding a canonical representative and an
  explicit unimodular conjugator (\cref{maps:src:F.2.36}, \cref{maps:src:F.2.37}).

For that conjugator $R$, the coordinate map $x\mapsto Rx$
  transports $(M_i,v_i,\kappa,P)$ to
  $(RM_iR^{-1},Rv_i,R\kappa,RP)$.  Since
  $(RP)^{-1}(Rx)=P^{-1}x$, it intertwines the specified cusp charts
  as well as the affine caps and clutch.  The resulting finite
  cellular cone and group presentation compute all integral homology
  and the full fundamental group (\cref{maps:src:F.2.31}, \cref{maps:src:F.2.35}, \cref{maps:src:F.2.39}).

The exact two-point survivor tests and the three-point
  orbifold quotient give the complete constructive parametrization;
  the separate involution branch has 56 classes.  The displayed
  unbounded trace family proves why the terminating bound depends on
  the supplied input (\cref{maps:src:F.2.30}, \cref{maps:src:F.2.38}, \cref{maps:src:F.2.39}).

Nine explicitly given complex-line directions and a uniform
  singular-value bound put a spanning tube in the unpolarized period
  domain.  The verified local-spray approximation theorem, with the
  relative extension-point argument proved here, produces a
  holomorphic transverse period section and retains any prescribed
  bounded cusp jet (\cref{maps:src:F.3.8}, \cref{maps:src:F.3.10}, \cref{maps:src:F.3.11}).

For a polarized abelian-surface source, semisimplicity and the
  maximal square-zero cusp force the middle rank-four system to have
  no invariant or coinvariant vectors.  The actual filtration
  $0\subset\mathbb Q\subset E\subset T$, with middle quotient that
  system and top quotient $\mathbb Q$, then forces both relevant
  invariant ranks to be one; the integral Euler-parity relation
  excludes $b_1=b_2=0$ (\cref{maps:src:F.3.4}).
